distinguishing_features: Applies a liquid-infused low-surface-energy coating to downhole casing/screen surfaces rather than dosing a feed stream or retuning a reactor temperature.
Reduces the critical adhesion shear of silica on the flow surface so existing wall shear removes incipient deposits.
Targets brine reinjection injectivity loss at the wellbore wall rather than fluidized-bed particle agglomeration.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to maintain injectivity in a silica-scaling brine reinjection well by limiting deposition on downhole flow surfaces.
parsed.viable_reason: It is testable and physically plausible because even correcting the Darcy-Weisbach arithmetic to about 6.6 Pa leaves wall shear above the assumed sub-Pa SLIPS detachment threshold.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 already teaches reducing adhesion/cohesion by surface-energy modification, so applying a known SLIPS low-adhesion coating to the fouling surface is an obvious transfer rather than a new mechanism.
